Playbook.name: Windows — Remote Execution via WMI or WinRM - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A process was spawned by a WMI/WinRM host process (wmiprvse.exe, wsmprovhost.exe, winrshost.exe) running a shell/script/LOLBin (cmd, powershell, mshta, rundll32, etc.). Triage question: is this remote code execution / lateral movement via WMI/WinRM, or legitimate remote management?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: WMI/WinRM remote execution is a common lateral-movement channel; a shell spawned by these providers usually means someone is running commands remotely.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: WMI/WinRM child
Signal.Details: process.parent in wmiprvse/wsmprovhost/winrshost spawning a shell/LOLBin.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the WMI/WinRM execution is legitimate remote management or lateral movement.

Step.name: What did the WMI/WinRM provider spawn
Step.Purpose: The child process and its command line reveal whether this is admin management or attacker execution.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.parent.name RLIKE "(?i)(wmiprvse|wsmprovhost|winrshost).*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, process.command_line, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: An encoded PowerShell or a download cradle spawned by wmiprvse/wsmprovhost = attacker remote exec. A known management script by an admin account is benign. The command_line content is decisive.

Step.name: Where did the remote execution originate
Step.Purpose: A network logon from another host just before the WMI/WinRM execution identifies the source of lateral movement.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code == "4624" AND winlog.event_data.LogonType IN ("3","10") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 1 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS logons = COUNT(*), users = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType) BY src | SORT logons DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: The network-logon source just before the execution is the pivoting host - contain it too.

Node.Condition: An encoded/download-cradle or LOLBin spawned by WMI/WinRM providers, especially from a network-logon source.
Node.Result: True Positive (Remote Execution / Lateral Movement - IR)

Node.Condition: A documented management script executed by an admin via WinRM.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-WMIEXEC-CHILD, INV-02-WMIEXEC-SOURCE to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the management task; close as false_positive.
Isolate target and source; open IR; scope the spread.
Reset credentials used; hunt the source's other targets.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A monitoring/orchestration tool using WMI/WinRM by design.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
